summary: Find finite-difference magnetic-axis candidates, evaluate a refined limiter contact and trace a closed normalized flux boundary from typed R/Z arrays.

capability: Combine critical-point screening, limiter contact and ray contour tracing.
operation: R/Z axes, node flux and limiter polygon -> O/X candidates, contact flux and closed contour
discovery.model: Central finite-difference eight-neighbor candidate screening, bilinear limiter contact and tensor-product cubic interpolating spline rays.
discovery.geometry: Strictly increasing R and Z axes with psi[R,Z] node order; limiter vertices are R/Z pairs; no axisymmetric reconstruction is performed.
discovery.boundary: Limiter vertices must lie strictly inside the rectangular grid. Boundary contact uses refined grid-line intersections and the signed maximum bilinear value; each ray requires a first strict normalized-flux crossing.

identity.relation: finite R/Z flux grid and closed limiter to limited magnetic topology and boundary
identity.direction: R, Z, psi, limiter -> O/X candidates, limiter flux and closed R/Z contour
identity.definition: Screen strict eight-neighbor minima of a central-difference gradient-square proxy, classify Hessian corrections, refine limiter segments against grid lines, then trace ordered rays from the primary O point.
identity.model: Finite-difference critical-point estimate, bilinear interpolation and RectBivariateSpline cubic interpolation with first strict q>1 crossing.
identity.geometry: R and Z are one-dimensional increasing axes; psi has shape (len(R),len(Z)); outputs use R/Z ordering and no hidden device constants.
identity.coordinates: Caller-declared length and flux units are preserved; the implementation does not rescale units.
identity.boundary: No extrapolation, fabricated O/X point, dropped ray or default contour is produced on failure.
assumptions: The supplied grid is rectilinear and finite.
The supported case has a nondegenerate O point inside a nondegenerate limiter.

inputs.name: psi
inputs.description: Node flux field in R/Z order.

inputs.name: limiter
inputs.description: Closed polygon vertices in R/Z order.
inputs.constraints: At least four vertices; first and last are closed or the first is appended; nonzero area and strictly interior to the grid.

inputs.name: angle_count
inputs.description: Number of equally spaced boundary rays.

inputs.name: ray_samples
inputs.description: Samples used along each boundary ray.

outputs.name: opoints_RZpsi
outputs.description: O-point candidates sorted by distance to grid center.
outputs.constraints: At least one row; primary O is row zero.

outputs.name: xpoints_RZpsi
outputs.description: Finite X-point candidates after signed flux filtering.

outputs.name: boundary_psi
outputs.description: Maximum bilinear flux over refined limiter points.

outputs.name: closed_boundary_RZ
outputs.description: Ordered ray crossings with an exact closing copy of row zero.
outputs.constraints: Every ray must have a first strict q>1 crossing.

preconditions: Axes, node flux and polygon are finite and shape-consistent.
A nondegenerate O point and finite limiter contact exist.
supported: Finite rectilinear grids, empty or nonempty X-point arrays, arbitrary closed polygons strictly inside the domain.
excluded: Degenerate Hessians, topology ties, extrapolation, diverted/SOL/strike-point reconstruction and device-specific constants.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for malformed, nonfinite, unsorted, degenerate or out-of-domain inputs.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when no valid O point, finite contact or ray crossing exists; numerical interpolation errors propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the operation is finite and noniterative.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result mapping is returned after validation or ray-trace failure.

python.signature: solve_limited_boundary(R, Z, psi, limiter, *, angle_count=80, ray_samples=1000)

example.description: Extract a finite limited boundary from typed arrays.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.equilibrium import solve_limited_boundary
r=np.linspace(0.0,2.0,9); z=np.linspace(-1.0,1.0,9)
R,Z=np.meshgrid(r,z,indexing='ij'); psi=1.0-((R-1.0)**2+Z**2)
limiter=np.array([[.4,-.6],[1.6,-.6],[1.6,.6],[.4,.6],[.4,-.6]])
result=solve_limited_boundary(r,z,psi,limiter,angle_count=8,ray_samples=100)
assert result['closed_boundary_RZ'].shape == (9,2)
example.expected: A finite mapping with O/X candidates, boundary_psi and an ordered closed contour.

scope: Normal finite limited case against an analytic quadratic field.
Lower/upper node and sample boundaries, polygon refinement and bilinear values.
Malformed, nonfinite, degenerate, out-of-domain and no-crossing failures.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct tests establish the finite typed-array contract and the analytic quadratic regression; they do not establish physical validity, mesh convergence or broader null topology acceptance.
known_limitations: Exact sorting ties and degenerate Hessians remain rejected.
The spline trace requires a valid first strict crossing on every requested ray.
Scientific review, rights and release remain separate decisions.
